sentences.text: The gist of accusation in this case is that on 05.01.2024, one Sonam Nath, who is the wife of the present petitioner had lodged a complaint which was registered as CR Case No. 571/2023 before the Court of the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Cachar, inter alia, alleging that the present petitioner with whom the complainant got married on 17.06.2023 had subjected the complainant to cruelty after the said marriage.
It is also alleged that the present petitioner was already married before his marriage to the complainant of the said complaint case to another woman with whom he had two children.

It is also alleged that during the subsistence of his marriage between the complainant, the petitioner had also administered some medicines to the complainant and caused miscarriage to her in the month of August, 2023.

Learned senior counsel for the petitioner has submitted that the complaint case filed by the complainant Sonam Nath is not supported by an affidavit and an averment to the effect that before lodging of the said complaint, she had approached the Police.

However, the said complaint has been forwarded by the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Cachar under Section 156(3) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 to the Officer-in-Charge of Silchar Police Station to register an FIR on the basis of the said complaint which is not the mandate of the law.
Learned senior counsel for the petitioner has also submitted that the petitioner and the complainant had stayed together all along for two months.
Learned counsel for the petitioner has also submitted that the petitioner would cooperate in the investigation, if he is allowed to go on bail.

Learned senior counsel for the petitioner has also relied on a judgment of Page No.# 3/4 this Court in "Tarun Dev Sarma and Ors. -Vs- State of Assam and Ors." reported in "2015 4 GLT 413" wherein it was observed as follows:-
"The provision, prescribed by Section 156(3) can't be read in isolation.

entities.text: Tarun Dev Sarma and Ors. -Vs- State of Assam and Ors." reported in "2015 4 GLT 413
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The same has to be read along with the provisions prescribed by Sections 154 and 155 Cr.P.C.
The decision held in the case of Sakiri Basu (Supra) makes it abundantly clear that prior compliance of the provision, prescribed by Section 154(1) and 154(3) Cr.P.C. is necessary.

A careful reading of the said statutory provision indicates that before invoking the power under Section 156(3), the party has to take resort to the provisions prescribed by Section 154 and 155 Cr.P.C.
A Magistrate, on receipt of a complaint under Section 156(3) can't act as a post office and just forward the complaint to the Police for investigation.
Any direction or order made by a Judicial Officer, in discharge of judicial work, must be a reasoned order.

Therefore, as held by the Supreme Court, in the case of Priyanka, a Magistrate exercising power under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C. has to apply his mind and record reasons justifying the need to send the complaint to Police for investigation.
It is also the duty of the Magistrate to ascertain as to whether the complainant has taken resort to the provisions prescribed by Section 154(1) and 154(3) Cr.P.C."
On the other hand, the learned Public Prosecutor submits that perusal of the case diary would be necessary for consideration of the instant bail application.
Hence call for the case diary.

4/4 P.S. Case No. 2470/2023, the above named petitioner shall be allowed to go on interim anticipatory bail of Rs.30,000/- (Rupees Thirty Thousand) only with one surety of like amount to the satisfaction of arresting authority, subject to the following conditions:-
(i) That the petitioner shall cooperate in the investigation and shall appear before the Investigating Officer;
(ii) That the petitioner shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any other persons who may be acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade such persons from disclosing such facts before the Investigating Officer.
